title: model-catalog: add capability flags and pricing/limits fields to capability endpoints; openai-compat & streaming stability fixes
author: Priya Patel
description:
Context: product teams need richer model metadata from the model-catalog API to make routing and routing-fallback decisions (e.g. streaming vs non-streaming, tool/function-calling support, structured-output schema guarantees) and accurate unit-cost estimates. This PR extends the /models and /models/:id/capabilities endpoints with capability flags, pricing and limits fields, and improves the OpenAI compatibility layer and streaming stability behavior.

What changed (single-string description): Added capability flags to model listing and capability endpoints: streaming_supported, tool_calling, structured_output_schema (string identifier), openai_compatibility (boolean/enum). Added pricing/limits fields surfaced in the API: pricing_per_token_infer, pricing_per_embedding, max_context_tokens, recommended_batch_size, rate_limit_tier. Updated query filters for the list endpoint: ?capability=streaming|tool_calling|structured_output|openai_compat and ?max_context_gte=<n> and ?pricing_tier=<low|medium|high>. Enhanced OpenAI compatibility mapping: parameter mapping for stop sequences, logprobs, temperature, top_p, and consistent handling of function/tool calling metadata (name/type/params).

Streaming stability fixes: reworked server-sent-events chunk framing to avoid duplicate newline/empty-chunk emission that caused some SDKs to mis-handle stream termination. Implemented backpressure-aware chunking and a short client-side jitter to reduce burst/connection spikes when many small responses are generated. Added retry metadata for transient stream resets and improved test coverage with flaky stream simulator.

Compatibility concerns: preserved backward compatibility for the previous minimal openai_compat flag but introduced an explicit openai_compatibility enum to indicate level (legacy, partial, full). API consumers who relied on exact response shapes may want to pin model version. This is documented.

Tests and CI: unit + integration coverage added for new capability flags, list filters, and OpenAI param mappings. Streaming integration harness updated to simulate chunked socket resets. Initial CI run showed a flaky stream test; rerun succeeded.

Commits (high-level):
- Add capability flags and pricing fields to model catalog schema and DTOs
- Wire capability filters into GET /models and GET /models/:id/capabilities endpoints
- Update OpenAI-compat adapter to map function/tool calling payload and new compatibility enum
- Fix SSE chunk framing and add backpressure handling in streaming handler
- Add unit and integration tests for filters, pricing fields, and streaming harness
- Docs: API reference updates and migration notes

Files changed (high-level):
- services/model-catalog/api/models_handler.go (add filters, new fields in responses)
- services/model-catalog/service/catalog_store.go (schema updates, DB migration)
- internal/openai_compat/adapter.go (param mapping and compatibility enum)
- services/gateway/streaming_handler.go (SSE framing/backpressure)
- pkg/test/streaming_harness/ (new flaky stream simulator tests)
- docs/api/model-catalog.md (reference + migration notes)

Expected impact: Enables route selection and cost estimates in Redwood Console and improves OpenAI compatibility for customers migrating from OpenAI-style APIs. Streaming stability changes reduce SDK-level connection errors during bursts.

Migration notes: DB migration adds new nullable columns with safe defaults; rollout will backfill capability flags from model onboarding heuristics where available. Customers using older SDKs should see no breakage but are encouraged to update to the next SDK patch for robust streaming handling.
